Firstly, understanding that AMD does not only produce GPU's, their Q2 report isn't too promising whereas Nvidia's is great. So I was wondering if the Gameworks thing had any effect at all? I've decided to swap to AMD, but Nvidia is still "top dog", so how do you guys feel about it?
How do you feel about Gameworks and AMD?

If Gameworks was just a tool to speed up the development of and implementation of the latest and greatest FX I'd be fine with it even if it simply ran faster on Nvidia components but its clearly not designed with that in mind. There is a lot of suspiciously inefficient use of tessellation and completely useless preemptive alpha channel (transparency) anti aliasing calculation going on that seems to be specifically designed to be dealt with by on the fly driver intervention to prevent wasted calculations, something that makes AMD's drivers look much worse than they are because each new game and each version of gameworks has different demands that AMD engineers have to get to grips with before an optimized driver can be released. (Nvidia has a long history of doing on the fly code substitution replacing shader code with code that runs really well on its hardware).

With that said AMD is at least partially responsible for its current situation, one of the reasons AMD GPU's have a high power consumption is because AMD set out to design a GPU architecture that does both GPU and general compute functions in one package, their CPU situation comes from their attempts to create a processor with more than 4 cores and save on transistor count ~ silicon restate for server applications. On paper all of this is great but the execution just didn't quite deliver products which were blowing people away like their Athlon64 and earlier HD Radeon were.

AMD needs to step up its game big time. You can't blame Nvidia for anything. They're just a company that runs on profits and they'll do what it takes to get more customers. And it comes down developers needing to make sure their game runs well despite the support they receive. I use Nvidia cause its good power for the price and Gameworks is pretty cool. And until AMD can provide a better value and experience i'll stick with Nvidia. It's not my job to support AMD with my money, it's my job as a consumer to get the best value and experience for my money.
Fair enough, what you say about being the consumer is absolutely true. However, I would like to point out that AMD has cards that match Nvidia performance wise at every price point.
